q: How is a cruise ship's CO2 per passenger night worked out?
title: Cruise ship CO2 per passenger night
short: Total the fuel burned on the voyage, multiply heavy fuel oil by about 3.13 t CO2 per tonne and marine gas oil by about 3.19, then divide by passenger nights. Some operators allocate by cabin area instead; say which method you used.
audience: Cruise operators, travel companies and corporate event planners

ul: Fuel consumption by type from the engine log.
Shore power used in port, as Scope 2 for the operator.

p: Crew and cargo are not passengers. If the ship carries cargo, split fuel by a stated rule before dividing.

example.title: Worked example (illustrative figures)
lines: Marine gas oil: 30 tonnes a day × 3.19 = 95.7 t CO2.
95.7 ÷ 1,500 = about 63.8 kg CO2 per passenger night.

senseible: Senseible reads electricity bills (CEA grid factor 0.710 kg CO2 per kWh for FY 2024-25, CO2 Baseline Database version 21.0) and diesel, LPG and gas invoices (IPCC 2006 defaults) into a dated, fingerprinted Scope 1 and 2 record for each site. Intensity per unit uses the activity count you enter, and estimates are labelled as estimates.
